sample_unit: adult musculoskeletal studies (2,926 radiographs) read by 2 radiologists

links.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) with versus without AI assistance in crossover design
links.effect: AI assistance did not significantly change AUC for fractures, dislocations, or effusions (e.g., fractures Reader 1 96.50% vs 96.30-96.50%, all p > 0.11); reading time fell and confidence rose.
links.quote: AI assistance did not significantly change performance for fractures, dislocations, or effusions.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in intended workflow versus unaided reading
links.effect: Diagnostic AUCs unchanged with AI; median interpretation times decreased (Reader 1: 34 s to 21-25 s; Reader 2: 30 s to 21-26 s; p < 0.001); confidence improved.
links.quote: Median interpretation times decreased with AI (Reader 1: 34 s to 21-25 s; Reader 2: 30 s to 21-26 s; all p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Comparison of three commercial AI tools against unaided reading on same studies
links.effect: Three AI tools compared with unaided reads on the same studies; no significant AUC differences, but BoneView gave larger confidence gains than Rayvolve and RBfracture.
links.quote: Confidence improved across tools: BoneView increased combined "very good/excellent" ratings versus unaided reads (Reader 1: 509 vs. 449, p < 0.001; Reader 2: 483 vs. 439, p < 0.001); Rayvolve (Reader 1: 456 vs. 449, p = 0.029; Reader 2: 449 vs. 439, p < 0.001) and RBfracture (Reader 1: 457 vs. 449, p = 0.017; Reader 2: 448 vs. 439, p = 0.001) yielded smaller but significant gains.

unlisted_practices: AI assistance to reduce radiograph interpretation time and increase reader confidence

screen.reason: The study tests the clinical practice of providing AI assistance to radiologists versus unaided reading in a crossover reader study, evaluating impacts on reading time, diagnostic confidence, and diagnostic accuracy.
